text:
maria: Heads-up — PTQ int8 canary (raven-lite-int8) shows a structured-output regression on funcall/toolcall JSONs. parse_success dropped and some tools mis-fire.

ajay: ugh. numbers?

maria: baseline float32 parse_success ~98.9%. int8 canary at 2500 samples -> 92.4% parse_success. funcall_mismatch ~0.8% -> 3.6%. latency down ~28ms median.

sam: any obvious tokenization changes or suffix truncation?

maria: digging — looks like streaming cutoffs and early EOS tokens for long tool outputs. also KVCACHE warm path appears colder (bigger prefix variance) causing partial JSON fragments at the tail.

jess: can we replicate locally with the same seq-len and kv prefix distribution? I can run a small replay.

maria: +1. ran a targeted replay with the same prompts and found int8 path emits an extra comma or truncated array close to 1.2% of traces. mostly when response length > 420 tokens.

linh: hypothesis: quant kernel shaves off a few tokens during the streaming buffer flush, causing malformed JSON suffixes. Another angle: decoding sampling entropy slightly higher -> extra commas.

ajay: what about retries/repair? We have the JSON-repair fallback in the agent layer, right? how often does it help?

maria: repair helps ~45% of the failed parse cases but not when the suffix is truncated mid-utf8 or missing closing bracket. repair adds latency and sometimes results in wrong tool args. Not great for correctness.

sam: propose a warmstart heuristic that prefixes a 8-token deterministic sentinel before the prompt on canary traffic only — to stabilize KV/cache alignment and streaming boundaries. We tried 3 variants in a local patch (0, 4, 8 tokens). 8-token warmstart bumped parse_success from 92.4% -> 95.8% on the same sample set for int8.

jess: interesting. what's the cost/latency delta?

sam: 8-token warmstart adds ~3-5ms median and ~10ms p95. tradeoff seems acceptable.

linh: also want to tweak retry policy: instead of immediate retry we should do a tiny exponential backoff and attempt a "json-wrap" repair that requests the model to re-output only the missing suffix. Patch idea: on parse failure try 1) local repair heuristics 2) send short retry prompt: "Your last response was truncated. Please output only the missing JSON suffix to complete the previous object." with max_new_tokens=150, temperature=0.0.

ajay: that second step is sensitive — could drift. Do we have telemetry to ensure we don't silently change semantics?

maria: we should only accept suffix-repair when the repaired text can be parsed and when a schema-level validation passes (types and required keys). Also add a confidence metric: if repaired tool args differ from original by >10% token-level edit distance, mark as mismatch and surface to ops.

ci-bot: [canary-run] 4159876543: started canary 1% traffic for raven-lite-int8 at 2026-03-21T15:04:03Z

jess: rollout idea: canary 1% with warmstart=8, retry_flow=[local-repair,json-suffix-retry], collect metrics for 24h, then 5% if schema_success >= 97.5% and funcall_mismatch_rate < 1.0% and no rollback triggers.

maria: added suggested metrics to the canary dashboard: schema_success_rate, parse_success_rate, funcall_mismatch_rate, suffix_repair_accept_rate, avg_repair_latency, p95_latency. Also added sample logging for any repaired outputs (store original + repaired + diff hash).

linh: small suggestion — measure "kv-warmness" proxy: fraction of requests that hit KV prefix cache on first 50 tokens. We'll instrument that.

ajay: do we need model-level adjustments? maybe subtle temperature/penalty changes for int8 kernel. But prefer infra fixes first (warmstart + retry).

sam: what about enabling a streaming sentinel that writes a final explicit marker like "\n---END-JSON---\n" after the JSON in the model output, but that requires prompt engineering on many templates. Could be a fallback for high-risk tool calls.

maria: caution: those sentinels change audit logs and some downstream parsers. prefer invisible sentinel (control tokens) if possible. We'll test both in isolated canary.

jess: can we push a small patch to the canary orchestrator to 1) add warmstart toggle, 2) enable retry_flow steps, 3) capture repaired sample bundle. I can drive the rollout.

deploy-bot: [deploy] canary-config updated: warmstart=8, retry_policy=[local_repair, suffix_retry], sample_rate=0.01 by jess at 2026-03-21T15:05:55Z

maria: preliminary stats after 30 minutes: parse_success up from 92.4% -> 95.9%. suffix_repair_accept_rate ~36% of failures, and overall funcall_mismatch down to 1.9%. latency p95 increased by ~8ms.

linh: promising. let's keep running for 24h. I'll start batching more samples for the eval harness: 10k examples across seq-lens to check edge cases.

ajay: long-term: if warmstart is required for int8 we should add it to the quantization onboarding checklist (PTQ/FTQ), and add a regression test that fails PRs when structured-output parse success drops below X.

maria: agreed. also updating the "model-onboard-playbook" with a kv-warmness step and recommended warmstart sizes per model family.

sam: follow-ups: 1) jess to run 24h canary and produce comparison CSV/plots 2) linh to run 10k eval harness 3) ajay to draft onboarding checklist change 4) maria to review repair acceptance thresholds and patch agent-level validation code.

jess: I'll post the canary report in #eng-ml tomorrow morning.

maria: thanks all. if p95 latency stays within SLA and schema_success >=97.5% after 24h we promote to 5%. If any metric regresses or we see semantic mismatches >1% we rollback immediately.

ci-bot: [alert] 4159876599: sample quota for canary repair logging approaching 10k — consider increasing retention or sampling throttle.

ajay: noted — linh can you prioritize which samples to keep (failures + repaired) so we don't blow retention?

linh: will keep all failures and their repaired pairs, sample 10% of successful parses for baseline.

maria: capturing action items in the ticket: INF-1429 (int8 warmstart + retry rollout + onboarding updates).
